results.note: Selections of Charlemagne's letters translated in P.D. King's 'Charlemagne: Translated Sources' (Lancaster, 1987) and Loyn/Percival's 'The Reign of Charlemagne' (London, 1965), both scholarly collections.
Charlemagne's charters/diplomata have partial English translations in P.D. King (1987) and Loyn/Percival (1965) scholarly collections, though no complete translation of all 'Diplomata' exists.
No English translation of 'Fragmentum adversus Sinleum' found despite searches of King, CCEL, Fordham Medieval Sourcebook, and scholarly databases.
No English translation of Charlemagne's 'Ad lectorem' found in any major source collection or database.

Selections of Charlemagne's Capitularia translated by P.D. King (30 capitularies, 1987), Loyn/Percival (pp. 46-105, 1965), and Ernest F. Henderson ('Select Historical Documents', 1896). Yale Avalon Project has only the 802 Capitulary.
No English translation of Charlemagne's 'Privilegia' (royal grants/charters collection) found despite searches of MGH, King, Loyn/Percival, and specialized Carolingian charter databases.

Attribution uncertain; medieval scholarship shows these carmina are often misattributed. If genuinely Charlemagne's poems, no translation found. Alcuin's poetry (with which these may be confused) appears in English in Godman's 'Poetry of the Carolingian Renaissance' and other collections.

Libri Carolini (De imaginibus) partially translated by Caecilia Davis-Weyer in 'Early Medieval Art 300-1150: Sources and Documents' (University of Toronto Press); freely accessible via Internet Archive at https://archive.org/details/earlymedievalart0000davi_f8u4
No English translation of 'Diplomata de Italia' found in MGH editions, P.D. King, or other major scholarly collections.
Another collection of Charlemagne's letters; likely covered by selections in P.D. King (1987), Loyn/Percival (1965), and other Carolingian source collections.
Mary T. Clark translated 'Adversus Arium' (4 books) in 'Theological Treatises on the Trinity,' FOTC vol. 69, Catholic University of America Press (1981).
No English translation of 'Contra duo principia Manichaeorum' found; this work is not included in the FOTC vol. 69 collection.
De generatione Divini Verbi included in Mary T. Clark's FOTC vol. 69 translation (1981) as one of the anti-Arian theological treatises.
Mary T. Clark translated 'De homoousio recipiendo' in FOTC vol. 69, 'Theological Treatises on the Trinity' (Catholic University of America Press, 1981).
No English translation found; attributed work of doubtful authenticity (described as 'a charming little treatise on the Creation and Fall'). Available only in Latin (Migne PL 8).
No English translation found; work of doubtful authenticity. Available only in Latin in Migne's Patrologia Latina.
Three Hymns translated by Mary T. Clark in FOTC vol. 69, 'Theological Treatises on the Trinity' (Catholic University of America Press, 1981).
S.A. Cooper translated 'In epistolam Pauli ad Ephesios' with introduction and notes, published by Peter Lang (1995).
S.A. Cooper translated 'In epistolam Pauli ad Galatas' ('Marius Victorinus' Commentary on Galatians') with full introduction and notes, Oxford University Press (2005).
No complete English translation found; the original Latin commentary on Philippians survives only fragmentarily (first 16 verses). No modern English translation identified.
No English translation of Florus Lugdunensis's 'Capitula ex lege et canone collecta' found despite searches of CCEL, Fordham Medieval Sourcebook, and academic databases.
No English translation of Florus Lugdunensis's 'Carmina religiosa' found.
No English translation of Florus Lugdunensis's 'Carmina varia' found.
No English translation of Florus Lugdunensis's 'De expositione missae' found; only Latin and French scholarly editions (Paul Duc, 1937 critical edition) exist.
No English translation of Florus Lugdunensis's 'Epistola ad imperatricem Judith' found.
No English translation of Florus Lugdunensis's 'Expositio in epistolas B. Pauli' found.
No English translation of Florus Lugdunensis's 'Opuscula adversus Amalarium' found.
No English translation of Florus Lugdunensis's 'Sermo de praedestinatione' found.
No English translation of Florus Lugdunensis's 'Liber adversus Joannem Scotum' found.
No English translation of Florus Lugdunensis's 'Liber de electionibus episcoporum' found.
Prudentius Trecensis's continuation of the Annales (835-861) is included in Janet L. Nelson's translation 'The Annals of St-Bertin' (Manchester Medieval Sources, Manchester University Press, 1991).
No English translation of Prudentius Trecensis's 'Breviarium psalterii' found.
No English translation of Prudentius Trecensis's 'De praedestinatione' (140,589 words) found; work remains in Latin only (Migne PL 115, cols 1009-1366).
No English translation of Prudentius Trecensis's 'Epistola ad Hincmarum et Pardulum' found.
No English translation of Prudentius Trecensis's 'Epistola ad quemdam episcopum' found.
No English translation of Prudentius Trecensis's 'Epistola tractoria' found.
No English translation of Prudentius Trecensis's 'Excerpta ex Pontificali' found.
No English translation of Prudentius Trecensis's 'Florilegium ex sacra Scriptura' found.
No English translation of Prudentius Trecensis's 'Sermo de vita et morte Maurae' found.
No English translation of Prudentius Trecensis's 'Versus' found.
